title: Level-One Fock Space and Residue Crystals

items.title: The symmetric-group level-one residue and partition-label convention
items.statement:
Fix $e\ge2$ and let $\Lambda_0$, $\alpha_i$ and $Q$ be the level-one data of the cyclic affine type $A_{e-1}^{(1)}$ Cartan datum of [[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]. This page works in the following fixed convention, called the *symmetric-group convention*, and every later item of the pair refers to it.

(i) *Residues and nodes.* Diagrams are English, rows increase downwards, and nodes are written $(r,c)$. The residue of a node is $\operatorname{res}(r,c):=c-r\bmod e\in\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$, and a node is an *$i$-node* if $c-r\equiv i$; the $i$-nodes of a partition are its addable and removable $i$-nodes ([[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]]). This is the residue convention of the level-one partition Fock space ([[def-level-one-partition-fock-space-and-node-residues]]) and of the modular signature ([[def-residue-signature-normal-good-conormal-and-cogood-nodes]]). It is the negative of Brundan's residue $r-c$; by Brundan's Remark 2.4(II) his normal rows of $\lambda$ are exactly the rows $i$ for which the node $(\lambda_i,i)$ is a Kleshchev-normal node of the transpose $\lambda'$, and the two conventions must never be mixed silently.

(ii) *The two label classes.* A partition $\lambda$ is *$e$-regular* if no non-zero part of $\lambda$ occurs $e$ times, and *$e$-restricted* if $\lambda_a-\lambda_{a+1}<e$ for all $a\ge1$ (equivalently: no $e$ equal column heights, i.e. $\lambda'$ is $e$-regular). Conjugation $\lambda\mapsto\lambda'$ ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]) interchanges the two classes. For $e=0$, Kleshchev's convention for the case where no non-trivial $e$-th root of unity exists, both conditions are vacuous and every partition is both $e$-regular and $e$-restricted.

(iii) *Crystal labels versus simple labels.* The vertex labels of the level-one crystal on this page are the $e$-restricted partitions, read with the modular signature of [[def-residue-signature-normal-good-conormal-and-cogood-nodes]] (i-nodes from top to bottom, cancellation of a $-$ above a $+$, good $=$ topmost normal, cogood $=$ bottommost conormal). The simple-module labels are the $e$-regular partitions, tied to the crystal labels by the transpose/sign dictionary $D^{\mu}\cong D(\mu^{t})\otimes\operatorname{sgn}$ of [[prop-p-regular-and-p-restricted-simple-labels-are-related-by-conjugate-sign-duality]].

(iv) *Conjugation dictionary.* The map $(r,c)\mapsto(c,r)$ is a bijection from the nodes of $\lambda$ onto the nodes of $\lambda'$, sends addable nodes to addable nodes and removable nodes to removable nodes, and satisfies $\operatorname{res}(c,r)=-\operatorname{res}(r,c)$. It therefore matches the $i$-nodes of $\lambda$ with the $(-i)$-nodes of $\lambda'$ as sets, and interchanges the $e$-restricted and $e$-regular strata. It reverses the top-to-bottom and the column orders of nodes.

(v) *Weight.* The weight function used throughout is $\operatorname{wt}(\lambda)=\Lambda_0-\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z}m_i(\lambda)\,\alpha_i$, where $m_i(\lambda)$ is the number of $i$-nodes of $\lambda$. Under conjugation $\operatorname{wt}(\lambda')=\Lambda_0-\sum_i m_i(\lambda)\alpha_{-i}$, i.e. the diagram automorphism $i\mapsto-i$ is applied to the weight; no weight is identified with $\operatorname{wt}(\lambda)$ without it.
items.strategy: Convention item. The residue $\operatorname{res}A=k_m+(b-a)$ with level-one charge $k_1=0$ is Kleshchev's (Kleshchev, *Representation Theory of Symmetric Groups and Related Hecke Algebras*, survey, arXiv:0909.4844, sec. 3.4, printed pp. 18-19, including (3.1) and (3.12)) and agrees with the library's Fock residue in [[def-level-one-partition-fock-space-and-node-residues]]. Brundan uses $\operatorname{res}_\ell(i,j)=i-j$ (Brundan, *Modular branching rules and the Mullineux map*, sec. 2.3, printed p. 3) and his Remark 2.4(II) (printed p. 4) is the explicit transpose/negation dictionary: his normal rows of $\lambda$ are Kleshchev-normal nodes of the transpose $\lambda'$. The $e>0$, $\ell=1$ identification of the $\tilde f$-generated set with the $e$-restricted partitions is Kleshchev's Example 3.2(i) (printed p. 20); the $e=0$ degeneration is Example 3.2(ii) there. The dictionary $D^\mu\cong D(\mu^t)\otimes\operatorname{sgn}$ is Kleshchev's Remark 5.5 (printed p. 25) and is consumed as [[prop-p-regular-and-p-restricted-simple-labels-are-related-by-conjugate-sign-duality]]. Clauses (i), (iv) and (v) are the elementary node and content computations $c-r\mapsto r-c$, addable$\leftrightarrow$addable and $m_i(\lambda)=m_{-i}(\lambda')$. Two convention warnings are recorded for Step 3 and for the cross-batch ledger: the gloss 'a partition is e-restricted when no column has length e' in [[def-level-one-partition-fock-space-and-node-residues]] is not the definition used anywhere on this pair -- the correct equivalent is $\lambda_a-\lambda_{a+1}<e$ (no $e$ equal column heights) -- and the conjugation map of (iv) is a comparison map between the two readings, not the sign/Mullineux involution of Kleshchev Theorem 11.8 (survey, sec. 11.5, printed p. 54), which acts by negating the residues of a good-node path inside one and the same restricted crystal. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Residue-node reading orders and the conjugation dictionary
items.statement:
Work in the convention of [[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]] and let $A\ne B$ be addable or removable nodes of one residue $i$ of a partition $\lambda$.

(i) If $A$ is strictly above $B$ ($\operatorname{row}(A)<\operatorname{row}(B)$), then $A$ is strictly to the right of $B$ ($\operatorname{col}(A)>\operatorname{col}(B)$). In particular no two addable or removable $i$-nodes of $\lambda$ share a row or a column, the top-to-bottom order of the $i$-nodes is exactly their order of decreasing columns, and the content $c-r$ increases strictly along the top-to-bottom order. Hence the content order of [[def-the-node-order-and-n-i-exponents-for-fock-space]] (larger content $=$ further right) is the top-to-bottom order, and the order of increasing columns is its reverse.

(ii) Consequently the $i$-signature read from top to bottom is the reverse of the $i$-signature read by increasing columns; cancelling a $-$ above a $+$ in the first reading is the mirror image of cancelling a $+$ before a $-$ in the second, and the two reductions have the same set of surviving nodes, with the leftmost surviving $-$ of the first reading equal to the last surviving $-$ of the second, and the rightmost surviving $+$ of the first equal to the first surviving $+$ of the second.

(iii) Conjugation $\lambda\mapsto\lambda'$ restricts to a bijection from the $i$-nodes of $\lambda$ onto the $(-i)$-nodes of $\lambda'$ that preserves addability and removability and reverses the reading orders: the top-to-bottom order of the $i$-nodes of $\lambda$ corresponds to the increasing-column order of the $(-i)$-nodes of $\lambda'$.

(iv) Consequently the modular rule of [[def-residue-signature-normal-good-conormal-and-cogood-nodes]] applied to $\lambda$ at residue $i$ and the Fock rule of [[thm-the-crystal-of-level-one-fock-space-is-the-good-node-partition-graph]], read on the column-decreasing order of $\lambda'$ at residue $-i$, have the same reduced words, the same surviving nodes and the same good and cogood extrema.
items.strategy: Elementary but load-bearing order lemma; it is what makes the convention comparison of the next proposition a term-by-term identity rather than a claim. (i) If $A$ and $B$ lie in one column, then both are on the boundary of the same column of the Young diagram and so are both removable or both addable only in the degenerate cases excluded by the definitions: in a fixed column the cells are the topmost ones, a column contains at most one removable node ($\lambda_r>\lambda_{r+1}$) and at most one addable node ($c=\lambda_r+1$ with $\lambda_{r-1}\ge c$), and an addable and a removable node in one column are impossible because addability at $(r,c)$ forces $\lambda_{r-1}\ge c$ while removability at $(r',c)$ forces $\lambda_{r'}=c$ with $r'\ge r$. For four cases ($A,B$ removable; $A,B$ addable; $A$ removable $B$ addable; $A$ addable $B$ removable) with $r<r'$ the same inequalities give $\operatorname{col}(A)>\operatorname{col}(B)$: $\lambda_r\ge\lambda_{r'}=c'$ with equality excluded; $c=\lambda_r+1$, $c'=\lambda_{r'}+1\le\lambda_r+1$ with equality excluded; $c'=\lambda_{r'}\le\lambda_r=c$ (as $\lambda_{r'-1}\le\lambda_r$ rules out $c'=\lambda_r+1$); and $c=\lambda_r+1$, $c'=\lambda_{r'}+1\le\lambda_r+1$ with equality only for equal row lengths and then the same column. The content statement follows from $c-r$ increasing when the row decreases and the column increases. (ii) is the standard mirror property of the $\pm$-reduction: reversing a word interchanges the segments $+\dots-$ and $-\dots+$ and interchanges first and last survivors; it is the statement behind the equality of Fayers' and Kleshchev's conventions (Fayers, *Partition models for the crystal of the basic Uq(sl_n)-module*, arXiv:0906.4129, sec. 4, printed pp. 10-12, the reduction of $\pm$-sequences and Lemmas 4.1-4.2). (iii) is the node content computation $c-r\mapsto r-c$ together with the order reversal of (i) applied to $\lambda'$. (iv) combines (i)-(iii) with the definition of the two rules.

items.title: The QG Fock-crystal arrows are the modular good-node operators
items.statement:
Let $e\ge2$ and use the symmetric-group convention of [[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]].

(i) On the $e$-restricted partitions the good-node deletion $\tilde e_i$ and the cogood-node addition $\tilde f_i$ of [[def-good-node-and-cogood-node-crystal-operators]] are defined exactly on the $\varepsilon_i>0$ respectively $\varphi_i>0$ vertices and give a crystal isomorphic to the level-one Fock crystal of [[thm-the-crystal-of-level-one-fock-space-is-the-good-node-partition-graph]]; that is, in the symmetric-group reading of the level-one partition Fock crystal the Kashiwara arrows are exactly the modular good-node deletion and cogood-node addition.

(ii) Explicitly, conjugation is the comparison map: for every $e$-restricted $\lambda$ and every $i\in\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$, the modular operator $\tilde e_i$ is defined on $\lambda$ if and only if the Fock-crystal operator $\tilde e_{-i}$ is defined on the $e$-regular partition $\lambda'$, and then $(\tilde e_i\lambda)'=\tilde e_{-i}^{\mathrm{Fock}}(\lambda')$; likewise $(\tilde f_i\lambda)'=\tilde f_{-i}^{\mathrm{Fock}}(\lambda')$. Equivalently, conjugation followed by the residue negation $i\mapsto-i$ is an isomorphism from the modular good/cogood crystal on the $e$-restricted partitions onto the level-one Fock crystal restricted to its empty component; its weight compatibility is the diagram automorphism of [[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]](v).

(iii) Naming dictionary. In the language of [[def-good-and-cogood-nodes-by-residue-signature-reduction]] the QG Fock 'good node' is the addable node selected for $\tilde f$ and the QG 'cogood node' is the removable node selected for $\tilde e$; with this convention, the QG good $i$-node of $\lambda'$ is the conjugate of the modular cogood $(-i)$-node of $\lambda$, and the QG cogood $i$-node of $\lambda'$ is the conjugate of the modular good $(-i)$-node of $\lambda$. The two sources therefore use the words 'good' and 'cogood' with opposite addable/removable polarity, and this item fixes the dictionary; neither convention may be quoted without it. Warning, recorded for the supplier's Step-3 author: the bracket recipe as printed in [[def-good-and-cogood-nodes-by-residue-signature-reduction]] (order by increasing content, cancel adjacent pairs $)($, good $=$ leftmost uncancelled opening, cogood $=$ rightmost uncancelled closing) describes the *restricted* reading and contradicts the level-one Fock module action; the Fock rule on $\lambda'$ is the column-decreasing rule of [[lem-level-one-node-order-and-conjugation-dictionary]](iv) applied to the transposed reading, i.e. cancel a $+$ before a $-$, with the selected $\tilde f$-node the *last* surviving $+$ and the selected $\tilde e$-node the *first* surviving $-$ (see also (ii) and the B-page counterexample).
items.strategy: The modular crystal statement is Kleshchev's: sec. 3.4 (printed pp. 18-19) defines the reduced signature, good/cogood nodes and the inverse property (3.13); Theorem 8.2(ii) (printed p. 38) identifies $(RP^\kappa,\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i,\varepsilon_i,\varphi_i,\operatorname{wt})$ with the highest-weight crystal of $V(\Lambda)$, and Example 3.2(i) (printed p. 20) identifies $RP^\kappa$ with the $e$-restricted partitions at level one; Theorems 11.6-11.7 (printed pp. 53-54) give the modular branching reading of the same operators (socle of $E_iD(\mu)$, multiplicities of normal/conormal nodes). The Fock-crystal side is [[thm-the-crystal-of-level-one-fock-space-is-the-good-node-partition-graph]] (batch-9 scaffold; Misra-Miwa Theorem 4.7 and Proposition 3.3, Leclerc Prop. 14, and Fayers sec. 2 Theorem 2.1 and the $n$-regular counterpart, printed pp. 2-4, with the $\pm$-reduction of sec. 4, printed pp. 10-12). The comparison is term by term via [[lem-level-one-node-order-and-conjugation-dictionary]]: conjugation matches the $i$-nodes of $\lambda$ with the $(-i)$-nodes of $\lambda'$ and reverses the reading order, so Kleshchev's 'cancel a $-$ above a $+$' is the mirror of Fayers' 'cancel a $+$ before a $-$', and 'leftmost surviving $-$' becomes 'last surviving $-$', 'rightmost surviving $+$' becomes 'first surviving $+$'; the two crystals have the same reduced words, extrema and inverse property. The naming clash of (iii) is unavoidable: the supplier's 'good node' is the addable $q=0$ node (Fayers' *cogood* position), while the modular 'good node' is removable. The recorded warning is not cosmetic: in the supplier's printed bracket rule on $\lambda=(2,1)$, $e=3$, $i=2$, the word $)($ cancels and the rule returns no arrow, while the Fock action has $F_2|2,1\rangle=|3,1\rangle$; the printed rule is the restriction-model rule and must be replaced at Step 3 by the column-decreasing rule above. Sources with exact locators are in the coverage file.

items.title: The restricted-partition component is the basic crystal in the symmetric-group convention
items.axiom_use: Inherits the axiom of choice exactly through [[thm-the-empty-component-is-the-highest-weight-crystal-b-lambda-zero]], which uses it to split an integrable module with a crystal basis into highest-weight components; the identification of the empty component with the $e$-restricted partitions themselves is choice-free (Kleshchev Theorem 8.2(ii) with Example 3.2(i) and Fayers' restricted model are direct constructions of the crystal on that vertex set). The choice-free alternative is recorded in the strategy.
items.statement:
Let $e\ge2$ and use the symmetric-group convention of [[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]].

(i) The connected component of the empty partition in the level-one partition Fock crystal, read in the symmetric-group convention, is exactly the set of $e$-restricted partitions, with the good-node deletion and cogood-node addition of [[def-good-node-and-cogood-node-crystal-operators]] as its operators and $\operatorname{wt}(\lambda)=\Lambda_0-\sum_im_i(\lambda)\alpha_i$ as its weight function. It is isomorphic to the highest-weight crystal $B(\Lambda_0)$; the empty partition is its unique source, $\varepsilon_i(\lambda)$ and $\varphi_i(\lambda)$ are the numbers of normal and conormal $i$-nodes, and every $e$-restricted partition is reached from the empty partition by finitely many cogood additions.

(ii) The whole Fock space is strictly larger than this component: for finite $e$ the partitions outside the empty component are exactly the partitions that are not $e$-restricted in this reading (equivalently, their conjugates are not $e$-regular), so the Fock representation is reducible and is not the basic representation. (For the boundary example see the companion page.)

(iii) Simple labels. Under the transpose/sign dictionary of [[prop-p-regular-and-p-restricted-simple-labels-are-related-by-conjugate-sign-duality]] the $e$-restricted crystal labels $\lambda$ label the $e$-regular modular simple modules $D^{\lambda'}$ of the symmetric groups in characteristic $e$, and the good-node deletion is the modular restriction operator: if $\varepsilon_i(\lambda)>0$ then the socle of $E_{-i}D^{\lambda'}$ is $D^{(\tilde e_i\lambda)'}$, where $-i$ is the residue (in the $c-r$ convention) of the node transposed to the deleted node of (i); equivalently the deleted node itself has residue $i$ in the restricted reading of (i).

(iv) Degenerate case $e=0$. If no non-trivial $e$-th root of unity exists (Kleshchev's $e=0$ convention) then every partition is $e$-restricted, the component is the entire partition Fock crystal, and no cancellation occurs; the library's affine Cartan datum is only defined for $e\ge2$, so this clause records the boundary case of the source convention and makes no affine statement.
items.strategy: Containment and the vertex set: Kleshchev's sec. 3.4 (printed pp. 18-19) defines the $\tilde f$-generated set $RP^\kappa$ and Example 3.2(i) identifies it with the $e$-restricted partitions for $e>0$, $\ell=1$; Theorem 8.2(ii) (printed p. 38) identifies the crystal $(RP^\kappa,\tilde e,\tilde f,\varepsilon,\varphi,\operatorname{wt})$ with the highest-weight crystal of $V(\Lambda_0)$; the uniqueness of the source and the reachability are also the content of the batch-22 supplier [[prop-every-p-restricted-partition-is-reached-by-cogood-node-additions]]. The identification with the library's empty component goes through [[prop-qg-fock-crystal-arrows-agree-with-the-modular-good-node-operators]] and [[thm-the-empty-component-is-the-highest-weight-crystal-b-lambda-zero]], which supplies the isomorphism with $B(\Lambda_0)$ and the nonemptiness of the complement; the AC bookkeeping of that theorem is carried in the axiom field. The equivalent model statement is Fayers' Theorem 2.1 $=$ Misra-Miwa Theorem 4.7 (Fayers sec. 2, printed pp. 2-4): the operators on the $n$-restricted partitions with the increasing-column reading form a crystal isomorphic to $B(\Lambda_0)$; this is the choice-free route to (i)-(ii). For (iii) the socle statement is Kleshchev's Theorem 11.6(i) (printed p. 53) together with the dictionary of [[prop-p-regular-and-p-restricted-simple-labels-are-related-by-conjugate-sign-duality]] (Kleshchev Remark 5.5, printed p. 25) and the residue bookkeeping of the convention item; the multiplicity refinements of Theorems 11.6(ii) and 11.7(ii) remain with the batch-22 pair and are not needed here. Part (iv) is Kleshchev's Example 3.2(ii) (printed p. 20) read at $\ell=1$, where the defining inequalities are vacuous.

items.title: Level-one global-basis transition polynomials in the symmetric-group convention
items.axiom_use: Inherits the axiom of choice through [[thm-the-basic-representation-global-basis-is-unitriangular-in-the-partition-basis]] (and hence through [[thm-the-empty-component-is-the-highest-weight-crystal-b-lambda-zero]]) for the decomposition of the Fock space into highest-weight components; the definition of the polynomials themselves and the pairing are choice-free. Consumers must carry the same assumption while it is used.
items.statement:
Let $e\ge2$ and use the conventions of [[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]] and [[thm-restricted-partition-component-is-the-basic-crystal-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]; write $M=U_v(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_e)|\varnothing\rangle\subseteq F$ for the basic component of the level-one Fock space $F$ with its standard partition basis $(M_\mu)_{\mu\vdash n,n\ge0}$ and lower crystal lattice $L$.

(i) For every $e$-restricted $\lambda$ let $G(\lambda)\in M$ be the lower global-basis vector indexed by the crystal label $\lambda$, characterized by bar-invariance and $G(\lambda)\equiv M_\lambda\bmod vL$; its existence, uniqueness and unitriangularity are supplied by [[thm-the-basic-representation-global-basis-is-unitriangular-in-the-partition-basis]] restricted to the basic component, and its label is the symmetric-group crystal label fixed by [[thm-restricted-partition-component-is-the-basic-crystal-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]](i). Define the *transition polynomials* $d_{\lambda,\mu}(v)\in\mathbb Z[v,v^{-1}]$ by
$$G(\lambda)=\sum_{\mu} d_{\lambda,\mu}(v)\,M_\mu .$$
Then $d_{\lambda,\lambda}(v)=1$, $d_{\lambda,\mu}(v)=0$ unless $\lambda$ and $\mu$ have the same $e$-core, and the support is triangular with respect to the dominance order as transported from the QG-6 normalisation along the conjugation dictionary of the convention item (conjugation reverses the dominance order, and the label transport is the transpose/sign dictionary, not the sign/Mullineux involution of the restricted crystal).

(ii) The comparison with the QG-6 standard-basis coefficients is the transpose/adjoint comparison: by [[thm-upper-and-lower-global-bases-are-dual-and-crystal-compatible]] the lower and upper global bases are form-dual and crystal-compatible, and the $e$-restricted label $\lambda$ corresponds to the $e$-regular label $\lambda'$; the lower/upper polarity must not be collapsed (see the strategy).

(iii) The *dual coefficients* $e_{\lambda,\mu}(v)$ are defined by the perfect pairing of the basic component: $e_{\lambda,\mu}(v)$ is the coefficient of the dual standard vector $M_\mu^{*}$ in the upper (form-dual) global-basis vector $G^{*}(\lambda)$ with $\langle G(\lambda_1),G^{*}(\lambda_2)\rangle=\delta_{\lambda_1\lambda_2}$. They are not obtained from (i) by reversing the index names or transposing the matrix, and the weightwise form-dual lattice is not identified with $L$.
items.strategy: Definition item; the existence and uniqueness proof remains with the QG-5/QG-6 suppliers. Read the QG-6 lower global basis off [[thm-the-basic-representation-global-basis-is-unitriangular-in-the-partition-basis]] (batch-9 scaffold; Leclerc, *Fock space representations of U_q(sl_n^)*, sec. 3.13-3.14, printed pp. 25-26, and Lascoux-Leclerc-Thibon, *Canonical bases of q-deformed Fock spaces*, arXiv:q-alg/9602025, sec. 4 Theorem 4.1, printed p. 4) and restrict to the empty component, rewriting the labels by the transpose/sign dictionary of the convention item. Two owner-direction warnings are built into the statement and must survive authoring: (a) the map $\lambda\mapsto\lambda'$ together with the semilinear involution $|\mu\rangle\mapsto|\mu'\rangle$ relates the lower basis at $\lambda$ to the *adjoint* of the basis at $\lambda'$ (LT Theorem 4.1: $G^{\dagger}(\lambda)'=G^{-}(\lambda')$ and $[c]=[d]^{-1}$), so the naive 'transpose the coefficients' comparison is wrong and the dominance direction in the symmetric-group reading must be recomputed from the QG-6 normalisation rather than copied; (b) the dual coefficients of (iii) are defined by the perfect pairing supplied by [[thm-upper-and-lower-global-bases-are-dual-and-crystal-compatible]] (batch-8 scaffold), never by renaming the lower coefficients. The $e$-core and dominance properties follow from LT Theorem 3.3(ii) ($a_{\lambda\mu}=0$ unless $\lambda\trianglelefteq\mu$ and $\lambda,\mu$ have the same $n$-core) and Theorem 3.3(iv) ($a_{\lambda\mu}=a_{\mu'\lambda'}$); the image of the dominance order under conjugation is reversed, which is why the statement records the support only after the transport. No other page may read $d_{\lambda,\mu}$ as a decomposition number without first specialising at $v=1$ and checking the Hecke parameter regime.

title: Level-One Fock Space and Residue Crystals — Examples

items.title: The charge-zero level-one crystal through rank four at e = 3
items.statement: At $e=3$, charge $\Lambda_0$, in the symmetric-group convention, the empty component through rank four has exactly the following vertices, one row per rank: rank $0$: $\varnothing$; rank $1$: $(1)$; rank $2$: $(2)$ and $(1,1)$; rank $3$: $(2,1)$ and $(1,1,1)$; rank $4$: $(3,1)$, $(2,2)$, $(2,1,1)$ and $(1,1,1,1)$. These are exactly the $3$-restricted partitions of each size ($1,1,2,2,4$ of them). The cogood-addition arrows out of these vertices are: $\varnothing\xrightarrow{\tilde f_0}(1)$; $(1)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_1}(2)$, $(1)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_2}(1,1)$; $(2)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_2}(2,1)$; $(1,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_1}(1,1,1)$; $(2,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_0}(2,2)$, $(2,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_2}(3,1)$; $(1,1,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_0}(1,1,1,1)$, $(1,1,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_1}(2,1,1)$; all remaining residues give $\tilde f_i=0$ at these vertices. The good-deletion arrows into the listed ranks are: $(1)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_0}\varnothing$; $(2)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_1}(1)$, $(1,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_2}(1)$; $(2,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_2}(2)$, $(1,1,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_1}(1,1)$; $(2,2)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_0}(2,1)$, $(3,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_2}(2,1)$, $(2,1,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_1}(1,1,1)$, $(1,1,1,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_0}(1,1,1)$. In particular $(2,1)$ has no arrow of residue $1$ in either direction, and $(2,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_2}(3,1)$ is the arrow whose conjugate is the QG-6 Fock arrow $\tilde f_1$ from $(2,1)$ to $(2,1,1)$.
items.strategy: Finite verification by the reduced $i$-signature, hand-checkable at every vertex. Compute for each listed partition and each $i\in\{0,1,2\}$ the residues $c-r$, list the addable and removable $i$-nodes from top to bottom, cancel $-$ above $+$ pairs and read the topmost surviving $-$ and the bottommost surviving $+$. For example at $(1,1)$ and $i=1$ the two addable nodes $(1,2)$ and $(3,1)$ both survive, giving $\tilde f_1(1,1)=(1,1,1)$; at $(2,1)$ and $i=1$ the removable node $(1,2)$ lies above the addable node $(3,1)$ and the pair cancels, so $\varepsilon_1=\varphi_1=0$ and both arrows vanish; at $(2,1)$ and $i=2$ the addable node $(1,3)$ lies above the removable node $(2,1)$, the word $+-$ does not cancel, and $\tilde f_2(2,1)=(3,1)$, $\tilde e_2(2,1)=(2)$. Residue labels are $c-r$ as fixed in the convention item. The list of $3$-restricted partitions is the direct check of $\lambda_a-\lambda_{a+1}<3$; the count $1,1,2,2,4$ matches the multiplicity of $V(\Lambda_0)$ (Leclerc, *Fock space representations of U_q(sl_n^)*, sec. 3.14, printed pp. 25-26, where the $n$-regular labels give the basic representation; the restricted reading is the transpose/sign dictionary of the convention item). No module theory is used beyond the vertex list of [[thm-restricted-partition-component-is-the-basic-crystal-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]].

items.title: The Fock E- and F-actions on the shape (2,1) at e = 3
items.statement:
In the level-one partition Fock space at $e=3$, with nodes listed by increasing content and the exponents $N^{r}_i$, $N^{l}_i$ of [[def-the-node-order-and-n-i-exponents-for-fock-space]], the node formulas of [[thm-the-fock-space-node-formulas-satisfy-the-quantum-affine-relations]] on the standard vector $M_{(2,1)}=|2,1\rangle$ give, with all other coefficients zero:
$$F_0|2,1\rangle=|2,2\rangle,\quad F_1|2,1\rangle=q^{-1}|2,1,1\rangle,\quad F_2|2,1\rangle=|3,1\rangle,$$
$$E_0|2,1\rangle=0,\quad E_1|2,1\rangle=q^{-1}|1,1\rangle,\quad E_2|2,1\rangle=|2\rangle .$$
The exponents are: $F_0$ adds the residue-$0$ node $(2,2)$ with $N^{r}=0$; $F_1$ adds the residue-$1$ node $(3,1)$ with $N^{r}=0-1=-1$ (the removable node $(1,2)$ lies to its right); $F_2$ adds the residue-$2$ node $(1,3)$ with $N^{r}=0$; $E_1$ removes $(1,2)$ with $N^{l}=1$; $E_2$ removes $(2,1)$ with $N^{l}=0$; and $E_0=0$ because $(2,1)$ has no removable $0$-node. Negative exponents and the $q^{-1}$-coefficient at $F_1$ are therefore unavoidable at this shape.

Warning (crystal reading). The exponents above are those of the standard basis and are not in themselves the crystal operators: the crystal is read through the lower global basis and its lattice, and the naive $q$-adic leading term of a standard-basis expansion can disagree with the crystal arrow. At this shape the symmetric-group crystal of [[thm-restricted-partition-component-is-the-basic-crystal-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]] has $\tilde f_0(2,1)=(2,2)$, $\tilde f_2(2,1)=(3,1)$, $\tilde e_2(2,1)=(2)$ and no arrow of residue $1$, whereas the standard vector satisfies $F_1|2,1\rangle=q^{-1}|2,1,1\rangle$; consequently $M_{(2,1)}$ and the crystal element labelled $(2,1)$ are not the same vector up to scalar, and the comparison of the two residue-$1$ answers must go through [[prop-qg-fock-crystal-arrows-agree-with-the-modular-good-node-operators]] and the global-basis transition of the definition item of this pair.
items.strategy: Direct computation, one line per residue: list the addable and removable nodes of residue $i$, evaluate $N^{r}_i(\lambda,\gamma)$ resp. $-N^{l}_i(\lambda,\gamma)$ by counting the $i$-nodes strictly to the right, resp. strictly to the left, of the node involved, and read the coefficient $q^{N}$ off [[thm-the-fock-space-node-formulas-satisfy-the-quantum-affine-relations]]. The calibration examples are Leclerc's Exercise 15 (Leclerc, *Fock space representations of U_q(sl_n^)*, sec. 3.10, printed p. 23): at $n=2$, $f_0|3,1\rangle=q^{-1}|3,2\rangle+|3,1,1\rangle$ and $e_0|3,1\rangle=q^{-2}|2,1\rangle$, which check the same sign conventions in the two-term case; the $q^{-1}$ in $F_1|2,1\rangle$ above is the same phenomenon. The warning is the standard distinction between a module action and a crystal basis: the crystal operators of the basic component are read from the lower global basis $G(\lambda)\equiv M_\lambda\bmod qL$, and $F_iG(\lambda)$ differs from $F_iM_\lambda$ by $F_i$ applied to the higher corrections, which can cancel leading standard-basis terms in $L/qL$; the two readings of the same label $(2,1)$ at residue $1$ are the smallest instance, and it is why the pair records the transition definition rather than an exponent-minimisation rule.

items.title: The full Fock space is not automatically the irreducible basic module
items.axiom_use: Inherits the axiom of choice through [[thm-restricted-partition-component-is-the-basic-crystal-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]; the exhibited non-containment facts themselves are finite checks.
items.statement:
At $e=3$ the whole level-one partition Fock space is strictly larger than the submodule $U_v(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_3)|\varnothing\rangle$, so 'Fock space' and 'basic representation' must not be identified. Two conjugate witnesses:

(i) In the symmetric-group convention the partition $(4)$ is not $3$-restricted, since $4-0=4\ge3$; by [[thm-restricted-partition-component-is-the-basic-crystal-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]] it is therefore not a vertex of the empty component, while $|4\rangle$ is a non-zero vector of the Fock space.

(ii) In the QG-6 reading the conjugate partition $(1,1,1)=(4)'$ is not $3$-regular, since its part $1$ occurs three times, so it is not a vertex of the empty component there, while $|1,1,1\rangle\ne0$.

The complement of the empty component is non-empty as recorded in [[thm-the-empty-component-is-the-highest-weight-crystal-b-lambda-zero]]; (i) and (ii) exhibit its elements on the two sides of the transpose/sign dictionary. Caveat: Kleshchev's signature rule is a crystal rule on the $e$-restricted multipartitions only; formally applying it to the non-restricted input $(4)$ (where the residue-$0$ word is the single removable node $(1,4)$) computes nothing about the level-one crystal and must not be used to place $(4)$ inside the component.
items.strategy: Two finite checks. (i) $4-0=4\ge3$ violates $\lambda_a-\lambda_{a+1}<3$, so $(4)$ is not $3$-restricted; the component list of [[thm-restricted-partition-component-is-the-basic-crystal-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]] then excludes it, and $|4\rangle$ is a basis vector of the Fock space by [[def-level-one-partition-fock-space-and-node-residues]]. (ii) The part $1$ of $(1,1,1)$ occurs three times, so it is not $3$-regular, i.e. $(4)$ is not $3$-restricted under conjugation; the $e$-regular description of the empty component is the QG-6 side of [[thm-the-crystal-of-level-one-fock-space-is-the-good-node-partition-graph]] as used in [[thm-the-empty-component-is-the-highest-weight-crystal-b-lambda-zero]]. The caveat is the restrictedness hypothesis of [[def-good-node-and-cogood-node-crystal-operators]] (Kleshchev survey, sec. 3.4, printed pp. 18-19, where the operators are defined on multipartitions but the crystal statement of Theorem 8.2(ii), printed p. 38, has $RP^\kappa$ as its vertex set); the formal $\tilde e_0(4)=(3)$ path is carried out outside the crystal.
